title: Compatible log morphism and affine toric chart comparison
statement:
Let $(Y,N)$ be a locally Noetherian fs log scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-trf-fs-log-blowup] with $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and a global chart $P\to N(Y)$ by an fs monoid $P$; write $\alpha:P\to A$ for its structural image [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $Q$ be an fs monoid and $g:P\to Q$ any monoid homomorphism. Write $\mathbf Z[T]$ for the ring of finite sums of monomials $z^t$ with $z^tz^{t'}=z^{t+t'}$. Form $C=A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q]$ using $z^p\mapsto\alpha(p)$ and $z^p\mapsto z^{g(p)}$, with tensor multiplication $(a\otimes u)(b\otimes v)=ab\otimes uv$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Assume $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$ is locally Noetherian, and give it the associated log structure $M=L_X(Q,\beta)$ for $\beta(q)=1\otimes z^q$ [lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks].

There is a morphism of fs log schemes $f:(X,M)\to(Y,N)$ whose underlying scheme map is induced by $a\mapsto a\otimes1$, and whose log map sends each chart element $p$ to the canonical image of $g(p)$ and every local unit $u$ to $f^\sharp(u)$. On any relative etale test $V\to U$ over $f$, it sends the local chart representative $[p,u]$ to $[g(p),f^\sharp(u)]$; these maps are compatible with restrictions and the structural maps. In particular the displayed $P,Q,g$ are compatible charts of $f$.

Put $B=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\theta:B\xrightarrow{\sim}X$ be the canonical affine tensor-product identification [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], with projections induced by $a\mapsto a\otimes1$ and $z^q\mapsto1\otimes z^q$. The comparison map $\kappa:X\to B$ determined by $f$ and the $Q$ chart satisfies $\theta\circ\kappa=\mathrm{id}_X$. Consequently $\kappa$ is an isomorphism and is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. No group-completion condition on $g$ or log regularity hypothesis is imposed, and empty $X$ is allowed.

source.place: VI 1.1, printed p.69 (associated-log chart conventions); VIII 3.3.8 and 3.3.11, printed pp.107--108 (log morphisms from chart base changes). Underlying comparison: Stacks schemes.tex Tags 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes, and 01JQ, lemma-fibre-product-affines; morphisms.tex Tag 02GI, definition-etale.

proof.text:
Let $i:A\to C$, $a\mapsto a\otimes1$, and $j:\mathbf Z[Q]\to C$, $v\mapsto1\otimes v$. Tensor balancing gives
$$i(\alpha(p))=\alpha(p)\otimes1=1\otimes z^{g(p)}=\beta(g(p)).$$
The displayed tensor multiplication makes $i,j$ ring maps. Let $f_0=\operatorname{Spec}(i):X\to Y$ and $h=\operatorname{Spec}(j)$. For an etale $U\to Y$ put $X_U=X\times_YU$. Etale base change makes $X_U$ an object of $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$. The stalk formula for the associated log structure identifies $Q\oplus_{\beta_{\bar x}^{-1}(\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}^{\times})}\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}^{\times}$ with $M_{\bar x}$. Thus $Q$ is a chart of $M$ in the stated definition; since $Q$ is fs and $X$ is locally Noetherian by hypothesis, $(X,M)$ is an fs log scheme.

source.place: VI 1.1, printed p.69; VIII 3.3.3--3.3.6, printed pp.106--107; explicit associated-log argument by Q04

proof.text: Write $\iota_Q:Q\to M(X)$ for the canonical chart. Set $H(U)=M(X_U)$ and $T(U)=\Gamma(X_U,\mathcal O_{X_U})$, with restrictions along the induced maps $X_{U'}\to X_U$. The etale base-change continuity statement shows that their underlying set presheaves are sheaves: the matching and gluing conditions are exactly those for $M$ and $\mathcal O_X$ on the pulled-back covering of $X_U$. Hence $H$ is a sheaf of commutative monoids and $T$ a sheaf of multiplicative monoids. Work on the small skeleton in the fixed larger universe. The structure map of $M$ gives $H\to T$.

source.place: VI 1.1, printed p.69; VIII 3.3.3--3.3.6, printed pp.106--107; explicit associated-log argument by Q04

proof.text:
For $U\to Y$, let $\alpha_U:P\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ be the restricted chart and put $E_U=\alpha_U^{-1}(\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times)$. The associated-log node identifies $N$ with the monoid sheafification of $D(U)=P\oplus_{E_U}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times$. If $r_U:X_U\to U$ and $s_U:X_U\to X$ are the projections, define
$$D(U)\longrightarrow H(U),\qquad [p,u]\longmapsto s_U^*\iota_Q(g(p))\,j_M(r_U^\sharp u),$$
where $j_M$ is the inverse units isomorphism of $M$. For $e\in E_U$, step 1 gives $\alpha_M(s_U^*\iota_Q(g(e)))=r_U^\sharp\alpha_U(e)$, a unit. The log axiom therefore gives $s_U^*\iota_Q(g(e))=j_M(r_U^\sharp\alpha_U(e))$. Consequently the two representatives $[pe,u]$ and $[p,\alpha_U(e)u]$ have the same image. The formula preserves products and identity, and commutes with restrictions because both $s_U^*$ and pullback of regular functions do. It is thus a natural homomorphism $D\to H$.

source.place: VI 1.1, printed p.69; VIII 3.3.3--3.3.6, printed pp.106--107; explicit associated-log argument by Q04

proof.text: The monoid-sheafification universal property extends $D\to H$ uniquely to $\varphi:N\to H$. Composing with $H\to T$ agrees with pulling back $\alpha_N:N\to\mathcal O_Y$: on $[p,u]$ both maps are $r_U^\sharp(\alpha_U(p)u)$ by step 1, so uniqueness in the same universal property gives equality on $N$. For a relative test $V\to U$ with $V\to X$ etale, the universal property of $X_U$ gives $V\to X_U$ over $X$; restrict $\varphi_U$ along this map. This defines the relative-test presentation of a log morphism $f:(X,M)\to(Y,N)$ with scheme map $f_0$. For a further test restriction the two maps $V'\to X_U$ are equal by their projections, hence the section maps agree by functoriality of $M$. Its value on a local representative is precisely $[p,u]\mapsto[g(p),f^\sharp(u)]$ by step 3; products with units and the structural maps are preserved. Thus these are the prescribed compatible charts. This uses sheafification over $Y$, rather than applying the associated-log universal property over the identity to a map between different schemes.

source.place: VI 1.1, printed p.69; VIII 3.3.3--3.3.6, printed pp.106--107; explicit associated-log argument by Q04

proof.text: The maps $f_0:X\to Y$ and $h:X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]$ have the same composite to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]$: on every monomial $z^p$ their ring maps agree by step 1, and monomials additively generate $\mathbf Z[P]$. Hence they determine $\kappa:X\to B$. The affine fibre-product isomorphism $\theta:B\to X$ satisfies $\mathrm{pr}_Y=f_0\theta$ and $\mathrm{pr}_Q=h\theta$. It follows that $\kappa$ and $\theta^{-1}$ have identical composites with both projections, namely $f_0$ and $h$. Uniqueness in the fibre-product property gives $\kappa=\theta^{-1}$, and therefore $\theta\kappa=\mathrm{id}_X$. This checks the specified comparison map, including both projections.

Since $\kappa=\theta^{-1}$, it is a scheme isomorphism. Its image is all of $B$, an open subset, and its structure-sheaf map is invertible, so it is an open immersion by definition. The open-immersion lemma makes it etale. All constructions above use only the tensor balancing relation and homomorphism laws of $g$; no assertion about $g^{\mathrm{gp}}$ or log regularity entered. If $C=0$, the same affine fibre-product isomorphism identifies $B$ with the empty $X$; section formulas and their sheafifications still exist, and the comparison is the unique isomorphism of empty schemes.
